criteria.criterion: Reproducibly download, verify official SHA256, build and install pinned PostgreSQL 18.6 into owned project artifacts without global packages or shell/home changes.
criteria.procedure: Inspect pin/download/checksum/configure/make/install paths and source scope; independently retrieve official SHA256, hash cached archive and installed binaries, then reuse exact verified install in isolated evaluation checkout per coordinator instruction.
criteria.observed: Official checksum retrieved over HTTPS matches pinned archive983ee...8ff3f. All five copied tools hash-identical to submitted install; psql/server report18.6. Candidate builds into project artifacts with make-j1 and optional integrations explicitly disabled; no global/home/shell change. Full native compile was not repeated; installed build and reproducibility commands inspected and exercised with fresh setup.

criteria.criterion: Provide bounded setup/start/status/stop commands for an owned durable development cluster outside artifacts; deny TCP listening, protect socket/data permissions, and never replace existing data or stop an unrelated process.
criteria.procedure: Run absent/setup/start/status/stop against isolated exact-candidate clone; verify private settings and permission/owner failures; safely test stale/recycled PID with owned dummy and symlinked runtime ancestor.
criteria.observed: Private socket,0700 directories,0600 owner, TCP disabled, existing-data preservation and normal lifecycle pass. However stale postmaster.pid pointing to owned unrelated Python PID83480 causes start exit0/already-running without PostgreSQL readiness. With stale socket inode, stop delivers SIGINT to that dummy before eventually failing. Status also follows symlinked development/runtime ancestor and exits0. These violate unrelated-process safety, honest readiness and symlink refusal. Setup configure/make and status psql additionally lack script-level timeout guards.

defects.title: Stale PID reuse can signal an unrelated process and fabricate readiness
defects.reproduction: In evaluator-owned stopped cluster, write signal-catching evaluator dummy PID to postmaster.pid. start exits0/already-running. Bind and close an AF_UNIX socket at expected socket filename to simulate stale inode. stop calls pg_ctl and delivers SIGINT to dummy (retained dummy-signal.json), then exits1. No unrelated user process was signaled.
defects.expected: Verify current PID executable, data-directory ownership, start identity and actual bounded readiness; refuse stale/reused/mismatched ownership before signaling. Do not rely on pg_ctl status/printed postmaster.opts or socket inode alone.
defects.observed: Python dummy83480 recorded signal2. pg_ctl status only uses kill(pid,0); its status output does not authenticate postmaster executable or data directory.

defects.title: Existing runtime operations traverse symlinked ancestors
defects.reproduction: With stopped evaluator cluster, rename evaluator development/runtime to runtime-evaluator-preserved and place a symlink at development/runtime pointing to it. status succeeds and reads through link; restore directories afterward.
defects.expected: Reject symlink components before any ownership/read/start/stop/data operations for existing runtimes, not only fresh setup.

defects.title: Command deadlines are not enforced across setup and readiness
defects.reproduction: Source inspection: configure/make/install calls have no deadline wrapper; status invokes psql without connect or query deadline. Only curl90s and pg_ctl30s are explicitly bounded.
defects.expected: Apply declared bounded command execution and readiness failure handling, with owned-child cleanup on timeout.
defects.observed: Native happy-path calls finished, but candidate does not implement promised bounds for these paths; pathological stall was not injected.
